sources.observation: The livestock depiction is possessed by the guardians and continues into creatures and the walking-frame image. This is not a facsimile inspection.

sources.kind: Kant, Idee zu einer allgemeinen Geschichte, AA VIII, lines 20–25; inspected electronic search extract
sources.observation: Another passage compares people with the sheep they pasture and refers to those sheep as their Hausvieh.

interpretive_decisions: Compose a sustained human husbandry role and a separate belonging relation rather than equating being an animal with being livestock.
Bind the depicted possessing group and the keepers to the same guardians; individual keepers need not individually own the subject.
Do not require residence inside a building. The separate pasture passage supports this choice but does not establish the unique meaning of the current metaphor.
Do not evaluate either the human-target description or the animal depiction merely because the author uses the metaphor.
remaining: husbandry roles, use purposes and the boundaries among domestic and captive animals
docility, confinement, walking and falling depiction
evaluative force and full source-equivalence review
